collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Nearly everyone at the assembly opposes a plan for different reasons: find what they share, or end without a decision.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The plan was to build a new fish pond. Half the village opposes it because of the location, a quarter because of the cost, and the rest because nobody asked them. (subject) is trying to mediate. (friend) is close to giving up. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) asks everyone what they actually want. It turns out almost everyone wants more fish, closer to home. The pond is moved, made smaller and built with everyone's help. Not everyone is happy. Most are.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The assembly ends in anger. People go home grumbling. The pond is not built. (friend) says the village will try again when tempers cool. Some people say it was a failure. (subject) says it was a beginning.
